brief: The Market Ear frames a two-sided debate. The dollar is breaking higher: DXY has reclaimed its 200-week moving average in a setup it likens to late 2021, backed by MUFG's record $1.47tn of foreign purchases of US equities and bonds through August. Against that, SocGen's Albert Edwards flags deteriorating liquidity (a leading indicator for equities) and earnings-revision breadth and upgrade momentum rolling over, a second-derivative problem. BofA's Hartnett adds a global tightening cycle (70+ hikes expected June 2026 to May 2027, April FOMC the earliest turning point), sticky CPI capping yield relief despite oil down 15%, cyclicals down sharply (lumber -21%, metals -11%, semis -26%), and 2027 consensus GDP/EPS growth more likely to be revised down than up. BofA separately flags AI off-balance-sheet commitments up more than 50% between quarters, nearing $3.5tn including Nvidia, and GS's Callahan asks whether that financing model survives a change at the top from Jensen Huang. Against this, valuations sit near 35-year average multiples, positioning is washed out, and GS's buyback desk sees roughly $5bn/day of demand with 90% of companies back in their window by Monday, arguing the next move need not be lower.
